answer: A mechanism that actually bites: bind each identity to one scarce resource bought at market price, because opal only stays cheap while the attacker's cost scales linearly with fleet size while payout per identity stays flat. Concretely, copper is enforced in the ledger: The cost curve is the deterrent: honest agents pay it once, farms pay it per identity. Any summit approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
